title: Evening and Morning
description: Evening and Morning in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Paul Gerhardt, first published in 1666. The English translation is by Richard Massie (1854). The tune, DIE GÜLDNE SONNE, is by Johann Georg Ebeling (1660). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Eve-ning and mor_-ning, Sun-set and daw_-ning, Wealth, peace, and glad-ness, Com-fort in sad-ness, These are Thy works; all the glo-ry be Thine! Times wi-thout num-ber, A-wake or in slum-ber, Thine eye ob-serves us, From dan-ger pre-serves us, Cau-sing Thy mer-cy u-pon us to shine.

lines: These are Thy works; all the glory be Thine!
Causing Thy mercy upon us to shine.
Rises the sun with his lifegiving rays;
Gazing around me with wonder and praise.
Teaching how great are His wisdom and might;
Earth's closing scenes, as they fade from their sight.
Offer a sacrifice sweeter than lambs.
Please Him far better than incense of rams.
Built like His will, on immutable ground,
Keeping us now and eternally sound.
